\section{Reduction to six proof-carrying branch formulas}

Let
\[
 f_0=(97,98),\qquad f_1=(97,99),\qquad f_2=(98,99)
\]
be the three edges of the unique seed triangle.  We first state the checked
dependency at the preceding deletion layer.

\begin{proposition}[Budget-five dependency]\label{fin:prop:budget5}
There is no \(F\in\cF\) with \(d_H(F)\le5\).
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}[Proof-carrying computation]
Every triangle-free \(F\) omits at least one \(f_i\).  In branch \(i\), the
unit \(\neg x_{f_i}\) is imposed and a sequential counter permits at most
four further deletions among the other \(826\) input edges.  All triangle
clauses and a finite bank of universally valid independent-\(18\) hitting
clauses are imposed.  The resulting three CNFs have respectively \(169382\),
\(184967\), and \(177799\) clauses.  All three formulas were reconstructed
clause-by-clause from \(H\), and all three DRAT refutations were replayed with
a freshly compiled checker from the pinned source revision.  The full
identities are in \cref{fin:tab:budget5-artifacts}; the formula-soundness argument
is the same as \cref{fin:prop:cnf-sound}.  Therefore each branch is impossible,
and the three branches cover every candidate of total deletion budget at most
five.
\end{proof}

By \cref{fin:prop:budget5}, a counterexample to \cref{fin:thm:main} would have exactly
six deleted input edges.  Fix any one absent edge \(f_i\) of the seed
triangle.  The other five deletions are counted among
\(E(H)\setminus\{f_i\}\).  Notice that the other two triangle edges are not
fixed present; if either is also deleted, it simply consumes one of these
five residual deletions.  Thus the branches cover all candidates and may
overlap.

For each \(i\in\{0,1,2\}\), let \(\Phi_i\) be the formula defined precisely in
\cref{fin:sec:encoding}.  It contains the fixed negative unit for \(f_i\), an
exact-five counter on the residual seed edges, all triangle clauses, and a
branch-specific bank of independent-set hitting clauses.

\begin{lemma}[Exact-six branch cover]\label{fin:lem:cover}
If \(F\in\cF\) and \(d_H(F)=6\), then the edge assignment of \(F\) extends to
a satisfying assignment of at least one of \(\Phi_0,\Phi_1,\Phi_2\).
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Because \(F\) is triangle-free, at least one edge \(f_i\) of \(T\) is absent.
Choose such an \(i\).  The chosen unit clause holds.  Exactly five members of
\(E(H)\setminus\{f_i\}\) are absent, so the primary edge assignment extends
to the auxiliary variables of the exact-five counter.  Triangle-freeness
satisfies every triangle clause.  Finally, \(\alpha(F)<18\) implies that each
installed \(18\)-set contains a present pair, so every installed hitting
clause holds.  Hence \(F\)'s primary assignment extends to a model of
\(\Phi_i\).
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Certified branch refutations]\label{fin:prop:unsat}
Each formula \(\Phi_0,\Phi_1,\Phi_2\) is unsatisfiable.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}[Proof certificate]
The three frozen DIMACS files have the identities and dimensions in
\cref{fin:tab:budget6-branches}.  The corresponding DRAT traces were accepted by
the pinned \texttt{drat-trim} checker, each reporting the exact status line
\texttt{s VERIFIED}.
Before replay, independent semantic checkers reconstructed the entire
triangle prefix, cardinality block, fixed unit, and every \(153\)-literal
hitting clause; they also checked the compressed and raw identities.  Details
are given in \cref{fin:sec:certification,fin:app:protocol}.
\end{proof}

\begin{proof}[Proof of \cref{fin:thm:main}]
Suppose \(F\in\cF\) and \(d_H(F)\le6\).  Proposition~\ref{fin:prop:budget5}
implies \(d_H(F)=6\).  By \cref{fin:lem:cover}, \(F\)'s edge assignment extends
to a model of at least one \(\Phi_i\).  This contradicts
\cref{fin:prop:unsat}.  Therefore no such \(F\) exists and \(\rho(H)\ge7\).
\end{proof}
